objectives.statement: Represent a multiplication as equal groups, an array and repeated addition, and explain why they show the same product.
Multiply a two-digit number by a one- or two-digit number with an area model, splitting by place value.

content.body: Synthetic school-supply demonstration. Each row has the same number of counters. The number of rows times the size of each row counts all the counters. Splitting a rectangular array preserves the total and exposes place value.

accessibility.textAlternative: Synthetic school-supply demonstration. Each row has the same number of counters. The number of rows times the size of each row counts all the counters. Splitting a rectangular array preserves the total and exposes place value. 7 rows of 4 dots: 7 × 4 = 28. Explain why each representation has the same total. Watch the rectangle split into tens and ones. Find 24 × 6 by splitting it into parts.

content.body: Both partial rectangles must be counted. Multiplication distributes over addition because the two non-overlapping rectangles cover exactly the original array.

accessibility.textAlternative: Both partial rectangles must be counted. Multiplication distributes over addition because the two non-overlapping rectangles cover exactly the original array. Find 24 × 6. Step 1: Split the first factor by place value. 24 = 20 + 4 Step 2: Multiply both parts, then add their products. 20 × 6 + 4 × 6 = 120 + 24 = 144
